The Venadu page says only that the Kollam Era 'instituted in 824-825 CE, likely marked the founding of the Kollam port'. Narrowed after review to the Kollam country.

predecessors.note: 1124: 'In southern Kerala, the medieval Chera dynasty was succeeded by the rulers of Venad (centered on the port of Kollam)'. This is the second beginning of the state's land: the Chera and Chola dossiers hold Kollam between 1005 and 1124.

successors.note: 1729: Marthanda Varma (r. 1729-1758) succeeds Rama Varma, 'the last Venadu king', and 'Venadu later evolved into the modern state of Travancore in the 18th century CE'. Kollam (the Desinganadu branch) was no longer Venad's: Travancore annexed it from 1731.

capitals.name: Kollam (Quilon)
capitals.note: 'traditional capital was the port city of Kollam'; Ravi Varma Kulasekhara ruled 'with capital at port Kolambam (Quilon)' (c. 1299-1316/7). The Venadu page also has a royal residence at Attingal from the 13th century. Span split after review around the years the dossier holds no land (1005-1123, the Chola and Chera hold on Kollam).

capitals.name: Kollam (Quilon)
capitals.note: Kollam again from the 1124 gain to the c. 1275 Pandya capture. Ravi Varma Kulasekhara later ruled 'with capital at port Kolambam (Quilon)' (c. 1299-1316/7) while the dossier holds no land (1275-1311, the Pandya hold).

capitals.name: Kollam (Quilon)
capitals.note: Kollam from the 1312 recovery of south Kerala to the end of Ravivarman's reign (1316/7, Ravi Varma Kulasekhara page); the dot moves to Tiruvitamcode in 1318.

capitals.name: Tiruvitamcode (Kalkulam)
capitals.note: 'at least during the 14th century, they lived at Tiruvitamcode in Kalkulam'; the pages opened name no seat for the later centuries, so the dot stays here to 1729 (Travancore's own capitals are in its dossier). The 1318 start is the year after Ravi Varma Kulasekhara's last attested reign year.

ledger.note: 825: Venadu is free of the Pandyas. 'It is proposed that the start of the Kollam Era, the Kerala calendar, in 825 CE' marks 'the liberation of Venadu from Pandya control'. The page calls it a proposal; under Varagunavarman I (c. 765-815) the Pandyas had 'conquered the Kongu country ... and Venadu (south Kerala)'. The Venadu page dates the Kollam Era 824-825 and ties it to the founding of the port. Review fix: the drawn land is only the Kollam country (the page: 'Venadu (based at Kollam or Quilon) came under Chera influence' in the 9th century; Kollam page: founded c. 825 as the capital of Venadu, 'a feudatory under the Chera kingdom'), not the whole southern Kerala part of the Pandya shape; the pandya-dynasty ledger 2 (825 loss, counterpart 'Venad') should be narrowed to match and use the slug venad.

ledger.note: 844 (bridge, the year chera-perumal-kingdom begins): Venadu is under the Chera overlord. Venadu was 'originally a chiefly territory within the medieval Chera state'; the page's dated sign is c. 849, 'the Venadu chief (the Venattadikal) Ayyan Adikal and his overlord, the medieval Chera ruler', and 'The first known Venadu ruler under the medieval Chera overlorship' (mid-9th century). The Kollam page calls Ayyanadikal Thiruvadikal 'a feudatory under the Chera kingdom'. Added after review; chera-perumal-kingdom has no mirror yet.

region.text: the Kollam country of Venadu, 'Venadu (based at Kollam or Quilon)': the Kerala part of a 60 km circle round Kollam, capped at 9.3 N (4,552 km2 on the grid, 8.55-9.29 N); narrowed after review from the whole southern Kerala part of Cliopatria's Pandya shape (18,462 km2, 8.34-10.70 N), which lay far north of the Venadu page's extent ('stretching from Kollam in the north to Tirunelveli in the south') and over the Chera Perumal kingdom

ledger.note: 1005 (bridge): the Chera overlordship over the Kollam country is cut by the Chola conquest of Kollam. 'The Senur inscription, dated to 1005 ... defeating the formidable rulers of Kollam (Venad)' (Rajaraja I page). The dossier then holds no land until 1124, although the Venadu page has the Venad royal Kumara Udaya Varma named in an inscription of the last Chera ruler c. 1102. Added after review.

1005: Rajaraja I's Senur inscription lists Kollam. 'The Senur inscription, dated to 1005 ... defeating the formidable rulers of Kollam (Venad)'; 'The Chola subjugation of Kerala can be dated to the early years of the 11th century.' The Venadu page says the Malabar Coast 'including Venadu, came under imperial Chola control by the late 10th and early 11th centuries'. The Chola dossier records the matching gain (ledger 15).

region.text: Venad from Kollam in the north to Suchindram or Nagercoil in the south, including Nanjinadu (the Venadu page)

ledger.note: c. 1124: Venad takes over southern Kerala as the Chera state ends. 'In southern Kerala, the medieval Chera dynasty was succeeded by the rulers of Venad (centered on the port of Kollam)'; 'In the early 12th century, the medieval Chera kingdom of Kerala dissolved into several local powers' (infobox end c. 1124). The Venadu page's first list begins Vira Kerala Varma at 1117.

region.text: Venad from Kollam in the north to Suchindram or Nagercoil in the south, including Nanjinadu (the Venadu page)

ledger.note: c. 1275: the Pandyas take Kollam. 'In the latter half of the 13th century, Venadu came under the control of the Pandyas'; Maravarman Kulasekhara is 'the one who destroyed the Chera ruler and captured Kollam' (c. 1275 CE); Venadu 'likely became one of the Pandya state's mandalams'. The Ravi Varma Kulasekhara page calls the Venad kings 'intermittently independent vassals of the Pandyas' and says Ravivarman 'ruled as a vassal' for more than a decade after 1299, so the loss may be a vassalage; pandya-empire draws south Kerala as its own land until 1312.

region.text: Venad from Kollam in the north to Suchindram or Nagercoil in the south, including Nanjinadu (the Venadu page)

ledger.note: 1312: south Kerala slips out of Pandya hands. 'By 1312 the Pandya control over south Kerala was also lost.' The pandya-empire dossier records the loss in 1312 (ledger 22) to 'rulers of south Kerala'.

1312: Ravivarman raids and crowns himself in the Pandya country. He 'started raiding the Pandya kingdom in 1312 AD' and 'performed his coronation at the Pandya capital Madurai (1312)'; he 'established supremacy over most of the region between Cape Comorin and Madras', 'as far north as Nellore', and was crowned again at Kanchi in 1312-13 where his hold was 'only short-lived'.

1316: Ravivarman falls back to Venad. Ravi Varma Kulasekhara page reread: 'Ravivarma ceded some of the conquered territory to the Warangal, and was compelled to withdraw to Venatu', directly after the Kakatiya campaign that 'defeated Vira Pandya and Ravivarman Kulasekhara at Tiruvadikundram' (early 1316) and 'captured the city [Kanchi] in sometime between March and June, 1316'. The page gives no separate year for the withdrawal and dates the end of his reign 1316/7 (a Kakatiya inscription cited there is dated 1317), so 1316 is the campaign's year, not a dated withdrawal.

Venad as Travancore inherited it, from Edava in the north to Aralvaimozhi in the south ('a small chiefdom extending from Edava in the north to Aralvaimozhi under the Venadu Kingdom', Marthanda Varma page): Kalkulam and Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram

region.text: Kollam and its country north of Edava (Jayasimhanadu or Desinganadu); the land from Edava south stays with Venad ('a small chiefdom extending from Edava in the north to Aralvaimozhi', Marthanda Varma page)

ledger.note: early 14th century (bridged to 1317): the Kollam branch forms. The Venadu rulers 'moved to Kallada, Kollam' and formed 'a separate family branch that ruled the region of Jayasimhanadu or Desinganadu'; by the 17th century Venadu 'had fragmented into several collateral branches'. The page gives no year; 1317 is the end of Ravivarman's reign at Kollam. The travancore dossier takes the Kollam chiefdom in 1731. [Reviewer g-sa-c, 2026-11-01: region bounded at Edava, minus keyframe venad_1317, so the split no longer takes the Thiruvananthapuram land that the 1317-1728 keyframe keeps.] Review re-check: the Venadu page still says only that 'in the early 14th century CE, the Venadu rulers moved to Kallada, Kollam' forming 'a separate family branch that ruled the region of Jayasimhanadu or Desinganadu'; the Kollam page (read for this) has no Kollam branch, no Desinganadu split and no 14th-century date, so the year stays a bridge.

region.text: Venad as Travancore inherited it (the 1317-1728 keyframe), the land that paid tribute to Madurai

ledger.note: 1635: Venad (Travancore) pays tribute to Madurai again. 'Later in 1635, Travancore stopped paying tribute to Madurai' and Tirumala Nayaka's armies 'forced Travancore to resume tribute payments'; the page also has Viswanatha helping Rama Raya's army subdue Travancore in 1544 'which had been refusing to pay tribute', so the tribute is older than 1635, and the Venadu page says 'In the 17th century, the rulers of Venadu paid an annual tribute to the Nayaks of Madurai'. 1635 is the nayaks-of-madurai ledger 3 date. Mirror added after review.

region.text: Venad as Travancore inherited it (the 1317-1728 keyframe), the land that paid tribute to Madurai

ledger.note: 1729 (bridge): the state becomes Travancore. The relation is closed here because this dossier ends; nayaks-of-madurai ledger 12 ends the tribute of 'Travancore (Venad)' in 1736 (page silent), so the travancore dossier should carry the vassal pair 1729-1736 (it has none). Mirror added after review.

region.text: Venad as Travancore inherited it, from Edava in the north to Aralvaimozhi in the south ('a small chiefdom extending from Edava in the north to Aralvaimozhi under the Venadu Kingdom', Marthanda Varma page): Kalkulam and Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram

ledger.note: 1729: Marthanda Varma succeeds to Venad and builds Travancore. 'Raja Rama Varma died in 1729' (the last Venadu king, his uncle); 'Venadu later evolved into the modern state of Travancore in the 18th century CE' (Venadu page). The page gives no month or day for the accession.

wars.name: Chola conquest of Kerala under Rajaraja I
wars.outcome: Chola victory: Rajaraja I's Senur inscription of 1005 lists the defeat of the rulers of Kollam (Venad).
wars.note: The page dates the subjugation of Kerala only to 'the early years of the 11th century'; the Chera dossier has the Cholas at Kollam c. 1097-1102 and the Chera Perumal kingdom surviving to c. 1124.

wars.name: Pandya conquest of Kollam

zones.text: Venad from Kollam in the north to Suchindram or Nagercoil in the south, including Nanjinadu (the Venadu page)

wars.outcome: Pandya victory: Maravarman Kulasekhara captured Kollam and Venadu came under Pandya control for the rest of the 13th century.
wars.note: Pandya dynasty page: Jatavarman Sundara I 'led his army ... to south Kerala' (c. 1251); the Venadu page's c. 1275 is the only dated capture of Kollam.

wars.name: Ravivarman's raids on the Pandya country
wars.outcome: Short-lived Venad supremacy from Cape Comorin to Nellore, lost when the Kakatiya army took Kanchi (March-June 1316) and Ravivarman withdrew to Venad.
wars.note: Ravivarman is said to have ceded some of the conquests to Warangal; the page's account of his death is inconsistent.

certainty.note: The pages name ports, districts and capitals, never a boundary; the Pandya, Chola and Chera frontiers in the south are approximate in every period.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (no row). The citing dossiers use 'venad' for three different spans and none agree on a founding date: pandya-dynasty ledger 2 gives Venad its freedom in 825 (counterpart 'Venad'), chola-empire ledger 15 takes Kollam from 'venad' c. 1005, chera-perumal-kingdom ledger 6 hands southern Kerala to Venad c. 1124, and travancore takes Venad's land in 1729. The pages opened treat Venadu before c. 1124 as 'originally a chiefly territory within the medieval Chera state', so the dossier starts at 825 (the Pandya page's proposal), loses Kollam in 1005 and regains it in 1124 to match the three citing dossiers; the Venad land in 1005-1123 and 825-1004 is therefore double-claimed by the Chera dossier (844-1124) and a reviewer may prefer to start the state in 1124 and re-point the 825 and 1005 events to chera-perumal-kingdom. Loss to the Pandyas c. 1275 and gain 1312: pandya-empire has no event for the 13th-century loss (it draws 'Tirunelveli and the Kerala coast' as gained in 1220 from unnamed rulers) and records the 1312 loss to 'rulers of south Kerala'; the Ravivarman page calls the relation a vassalage, so a gap-filler should decide between loss and vassal_start/vassal_end in pandya-empire. nayaks-of-madurai ledger 3 and 12 name 'Travancore (Venad)' as a tribute-payer 1635-1736 and the Venadu page has the 16th-century rulers acknowledging Vijayanagara and Devaraya II (from 1426) subjugating Kollam's ruler: those vassal relations belong to the overlords' dossiers and the counterpart string should be 'venad' (or 'travancore' after 1729). The Venadu page gives two inconsistent regnal lists (e.g. Vira Kerala Varma 1117-1145 in one, Padmanabha Martanda Varma c. 1240-c. 1253 in the other), so no rulers strip is given. The Desinganadu (Kollam) branch needs a dossier or a nobody/neighbour treatment: travancore ledger 1 names it 'Kollam (Quilon) chiefdom' (1731). Desinganadu is a gazetteer-free name; places used are in the gazetteer (Kollam, Nagercoil). Elayadathu Swaroopam (Kottarakkara) and Kayamkulam also need dossiers. The Wikipedia title was returned by the tool as 'Venadu'. REVIEW FIXES (2026-11-01): (1) the 825 shape and found event now draw only the Kollam country (4,552 km2) instead of the southern Kerala part of the Pandya shape (18,462 km2), and the Chera relation is a vassal pair 844-1005 with chera-perumal-kingdom (Venadu page: 'originally a chiefly territory within the medieval Chera state'; c. 849 Ayyan Adikal under 'his overlord, the medieval Chera ruler'); the 844 start is the Chera dossier's own start year (bridge), and the Venadu page has the Venad royal Kumara Udaya Varma in a Chera inscription of c. 1102, so the vassalage plausibly lasted to the end of the Chera state although the dossier holds no land 1005-1123. (2) vassal pair 1635-1729 with nayaks-of-madurai (the Nayak page dates only the 1635 resumption; the tribute is older, 1544 page). (3) the capital is split around the years without land (1005-1123 and 1275-1311). (4) 1316 occupation_end raised to confidence 2; the 1317 split stays a bridge (Kollam page silent). Routing for other batches: pandya-dynasty ledger 2 counterpart venad and a narrowed 825 loss region; chera-perumal-kingdom vassal pair for venad 844-1005; nayaks-of-madurai ledgers 3 and 12 should use venad (1635-1729) then travancore (1729-1736), and travancore should carry the 1729-1736 tribute pair; pandya-empire has no 1275 Kollam event or 1312-1316 occupation pair; chola-empire's Cliopatria shapes still cover Kollam and Nagercoil to 1176. Gazetteer-free names: none new.
